message.content:
The function attempts to handle IPv6 address compression (the `::` notation) by recording the position of the double colon and then shifting the parsed bytes to the end of the 16-byte buffer.

Looking at line 8: `colonp = --tp;`.
`tp` is initialized to `tmp` (line 4). If `src` starts with `::`, `tp` is decremented. This makes `tp` point to `tmp[-1]`.
When `colonp` is used in `memmove` (line 21) and `memset` (line 22), it uses an address that is outside the bounds of the `tmp` array (specifically, one byte before the start of the array). This is an out-of-bounds memory access (buffer underflow).

Furthermore, the logic for calculating the shift and the number of bytes to move is flawed, but the immediate memory corruption occurs because `colonp` is set to an invalid address.

Answer: 8
